newsitem.title: USA: U.S. consumer credit growth leveled off in December.
newsitem.headline: U.S. consumer credit growth leveled off in December.

text.p: Consumers curbed buying on credit in December, a report Friday from the Federal Reserve showed, notably reining in their purchases on credit cards.
Total U.S. consumer credit still increased by $4.9 billion at a 4.9 percent annual rate but that was down modestly from a revised $5.1 billion rise in November at a 5.1 percent annual rate.
It also was less than forecast by Wall Street economists who had foreseen a $6.7 billion rise in the value of December instalment credit owed.
Furthermore, November's total of consumer instalment credit outstanding was revised down from a previously reported $7.4 billion increase.

The apparent leveling off in consumer instalment credit was notable since it occurred amid the height of the Christmas holiday shopping season. It was consistent with other indications that consumers were attempting to save more from their rising incomes.

The Commerce Department said Monday that personal incomes had risen 0.8 percent in December but spending grew by only 0.5 percent. Consumers boosted their savings to 5.4 cents out of each dollar earned from 5.1 cents in November.
The Fed said that, during December, growth in revolving or credit-card credit slowed to a $2.4 billion rise at a 6.2 percent annual rate from $4 billion at a 10.6 percent rate in November.
But automobile credit outstanding picked up to a $600 million rise at a 1.9 percent annual rate in December after falling in November by $100 million at a 0.3 percent annual rate.

Other credit, which includes consumer bank loans like those for mobile homes and to pay for education but not real estate mortgages, grew by $1.8 billion at a 6.3 percent annual rate in December. That was up from November when this category of credit advanced $1.2 billion at a 3.9 percent annual rate.
Before seasonal adjustment, total outstanding consumer credit in December was $1.23 trillion, up from $1.13 trillion a year earlier in December 1995.
